1.explanation:
1. audits/dobetterweb/js-libraries-test.js: Contains the unit tests for the JS library–detection audit, where version.match is called.
2. audits/dobetterweb/no-vulnerable-libraries-test.js: Closely related audit that flags known vulnerable libraries and shares detection logic.
3. audits/errors-in-console-test.js: Shows how console exceptions (like version.match errors) are captured and reported as a separate audit failure.
4. network-records-to-devtools-log.js: Converts recorded network traffic into the artifacts the JS-libraries audit uses to identify script URLs and extract version info.
5. runner-test.js: Orchestrates running all audits end to end—helpful to reproduce the error in a full run versus the isolated unit test.
6. index-test.js: Illustrates how the CLI/web entry point initializes and invokes each audit, so you can trace where an uncaught exception bubbles out to the UI.
1.bug_scenario: When running the “Avoids front-end JavaScript libraries with known security vulnerabilities” audit against a Magento 2 site that’s using require.js and their own bundled JS, the audit code calls version.match(...) on the detected library version—but in some cases the “version” value isn’t a string (it may be an object or undefined), so calling match throws “version.match is not a function.”  In the screenshot you can see the top‐level “?” error badge on that audit, and the console shows the thrown exception.  Because that exception bubbles up, the audit ends in an Error state instead of a proper Fail, and you also see the downstream “Browser errors were logged to the console” audit failing.
